skill.name: amazon-best-selling-products-finder-api-skill
skill.description: Run a BrowserAct workflow to collect Amazon product titles, prices, ratings, reviews, sales indicators, availability, promotions, badges, and links by keyword.
skill.summary: Collect structured Amazon product data by keyword and marketplace through BrowserAct.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill deliberately contacts BrowserAct and runs a bundled Python script. Most secret, backtick, URL, and reconnaissance alerts are contextual false positives. However, it encourages API key disclosure and forwards an unrestricted marketplace URL to the remote workflow.

remediation.issue: The instructions invite users to provide their BrowserAct API key to the agent.
remediation.suggestion: Tell users to set BROWSERACT_API_KEY locally. Never request, echo, or accept credentials in chat.

remediation.issue: The marketplace URL is forwarded to BrowserAct without destination validation.
remediation.suggestion: Require HTTPS and allow only supported Amazon marketplace hostnames before submitting the workflow.

remediation.issue: The documented workflow invokes a local script with user-selected arguments.
remediation.suggestion: Invoke Python without a shell and pass every user value as a separate argument.

content.value_statement: Amazon product research can require slow, repetitive browsing. This skill runs a BrowserAct workflow to collect structured listing, price, rating, sales, and availability data.
actual_capabilities: Submits a BrowserAct workflow with a keyword, result limit, and marketplace URL.
Polls task status every ten seconds for up to five minutes.
Reports workflow progress, failure, cancellation, connection errors, and authorization guidance.
Requests product titles, brands, prices, ratings, reviews, sales indicators, availability, promotions, ASINs, categories, badges, and links.
Supports regional Amazon marketplace URLs supplied through a command argument.
limitations: Requires Python, internet access, a BrowserAct account, and a valid BROWSERACT_API_KEY.
Sends search terms, limits, and marketplace URLs to the third-party BrowserAct service.
Does not restrict the marketplace argument to supported Amazon domains.
The current script exits after polling, making its result retrieval block unreachable.

use_cases.title: Research Product Categories
use_cases.description: Collect current listing details for a keyword before evaluating demand, price ranges, and review competition.

use_cases.title: Compare Regional Offers
use_cases.description: Run equivalent searches across Amazon regions to compare prices, availability, promotions, and badges.

use_cases.title: Review Competitor Listings
use_cases.description: Gather product identifiers and visible sales indicators for a focused competitor comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Find Popular Products
prompt_templates.prompt: Find ten best-selling wireless keyboards on Amazon US. Summarize title, current price, rating, review count, and availability.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Product Offers
prompt_templates.prompt: Collect twenty insulated water bottles from Amazon UK. Compare current price, list price, promotions, ratings, and past-month sales indicators.

prompt_templates.title: Assess Category Competition
prompt_templates.prompt: Research thirty running shoes on Amazon Germany. Rank listings by rating and review count, then identify common brands, badges, and price bands.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Regional Comparison
prompt_templates.prompt: Run matching laptop-stand searches for Amazon US and UK. Compare product overlap, converted price ranges, availability, promotions, and rating strength.

output: A ranked listing summary covering prices, promotions, ratings, reviews, availability, and brands.
A concise note identifying common price bands and highly reviewed options.

output_examples.input: Review running shoe listings across Amazon US and Germany.
output: Separate regional result tables with consistent product fields.
A comparison of assortment, availability, promotions, badges, and rating patterns.

best_practices: Set BROWSERACT_API_KEY in the local environment instead of sharing it in a prompt.
Use a supported Amazon marketplace hostname for the intended region.
Begin with a small result limit, verify relevance, then expand the search.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into prompts, messages, logs, or command arguments.
Do not treat one collection as historical trend data without repeated timestamped runs.
Do not use arbitrary non-Amazon destinations as the marketplace URL.

faq.question: What credentials does this skill require?
faq.answer: It requires a BrowserAct API key stored locally as BROWSERACT_API_KEY.

faq.question: Which Amazon regions are supported?
faq.answer: The script accepts a marketplace URL, but actual regional support depends on the BrowserAct workflow.

faq.question: What product fields can it request?
faq.answer: It requests titles, brands, prices, ratings, reviews, sales indicators, availability, promotions, ASINs, categories, badges, and product links.

faq.question: How long can a request take?
faq.answer: The script polls for up to five minutes and reports status every ten seconds.

faq.question: Does it provide historical price trends?
faq.answer: No. Each run collects current workflow results, so historical analysis requires repeated timestamped collections.

faq.question: Does the current script return completed results?
faq.answer: No. An unconditional return after polling makes the result retrieval block unreachable until the author fixes the control flow.
